clue.text: Something sharp that's taken from a doll

indicators.note: the doll's name has its last letters removed, leaving only the front part

parts.note: Barbie is the famous fashion doll

explanation.surface: A pointed object has been confiscated from a child's doll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' drops IE from BARBIE, the fashion doll, to leave BARB.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a sharp backward-pointing projection, as on a hook or an arrow.

clue.text: Caught in the confusion of racial distinction

indicators.note: a confusion of letters is a jumble, so these two short words are mixed up

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is tangled up in muddled thinking about race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles IN and THE into ETHNI; C (caught) then goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic describes a group distinguished by shared race, culture or descent, so it is a matter of racial distinction.

clue.text: America's not half keeping up fuel consumed? Improve!

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the shortened word contains the next piece
not half is read loosely as 'only half', so just the front of the country's name is kept

parts.note: the country's name, America, the 's being a link

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a fuel
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A grumble that America is barely keeping up with its fuel use, with a call for things to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' gives AMER, its front half; 'up' turns OIL to LIO inside it. The surface's 'not half' sounds like an emphatic British 'not half!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make or become better, a formal synonym for improving.

clue.text: Mind of spy working on insurgent

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work and moved about

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary insurgent

explanation.surface: A spy is studying the thoughts of a rebel he is assigned to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges SPY to PSY, followed by CHE, the guerrilla leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, from the Greek word for breath or spirit.

clue.text: Spooner's friendly greeting is anything but

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words change places

parts.note: mate is a friendly form of address
hail is a greeting, as in 'Hail, friend'

explanation.surface: A friendly hello that turns out to be its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of MATE HAIL gives HATE MAIL, abusive letters that are anything but a friendly greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile or abusive letters are the opposite of a friendly greeting, so the phrase means the reverse of one.

clue.text: Case for retention of the tuition fee

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters within it, so they are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An argument for keeping university tuition charges.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'thE TUItion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Trade in old coins

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
loose coins are change

explanation.surface: Dealing in antique coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to give one thing and receive another, which is what trading means.

clue.text: A name on this? Not likely!

definitions.text: A name on this? Not likely!

explanation.surface: Doubting that anyone will sign their name to this.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter signed 'Anon' is anonymous, so a name on it is not likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, is the attribution used when no author's name is given.

clue.text: Song about times out of joint involved in 14 production

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: out of joint means dislocated, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A tune about troubled times is part of making a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of joint' makes TEMIS. Clue 14 is ABSINTH, distilled from wormwood, whose botanical genus is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is the plant genus of wormwood, the herb used in making absinth.

clue.text: Poison from canned beef

annotationWithheld.why: Poison from canned beef (5): TOXIN is OX inside TIN, but 'canned' must give TIN and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Rusticate a student for being trivial

parts.note: to rusticate is to send down from university for a time, a kind of ban
L is the learner sign, a crossword convention for a student

explanation.surface: Suspending a student for doing something trifling.
explanation.walkthrough: Rusticate is a British university term for sending a student away for a time as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite or commonplace, so something banal is trivial.

clue.text: Unusual hop insect formerly found near Baghdad

indicators.note: unusual means not in its normal state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd hopping bug once seen around Baghdad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges HOP INSECT; the 'insect' is no creature but a ruined city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ctesiphon was an ancient Parthian and Persian capital on the Tigris, its ruins lying close to Baghdad.

clue.text: Little creatures steal in, being too small to notice

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the theft goes into the creatures

parts.note: mice are little creatures
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Tiny animals creep in to thieve, escaping notice because they are so small.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microscopic organism, a living being too small to see with the naked eye.

clue.text: Little time to get tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Only a moment to grab a cuppa, whether tea or coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea' looks like a rival definition but is CHA; 'coffee' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Ban this unruly intoxicant!

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: A demand to prohibit this troublesome drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong aniseed-flavoured spirit, an intoxicating liquor once banned in many countries.

clue.text: Store said to deal in white goods

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to deal in white goods is to sell fridges

explanation.surface: A shop is reported to trade in household appliances.
explanation.walkthrough: SELFRIDGES is a large London department store; 'sell fridges' sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfridges is a famous department store on Oxford Street in London.

clue.text: Heartless old king has heir to tea

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Henry was the name of eight English kings
a son is an heir

explanation.surface: A gutless former monarch leaves his heir a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry was the name of eight English kings; 'Heartless' keeps only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyson is a Chinese green tea, a variety of the drink.

clue.text: Order, mostly seen in this clue

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept and its tail cut off

parts.note: a command is an order

explanation.surface: A remark that an instruction can largely be found in this very clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark after 'Order' is the answer itself, seen in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark of that kind sits just after the first word, so one is literally visible in the clue.

clue.text: Log mania destroyed arboreal specimen

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A craze for cutting logs wrecked a fine tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub, so a single one is a specimen of a tree.

clue.text: Everyone said it's boring

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody says it's dull.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes, so it bores through material.

clue.text: Patronage instils piquancy down under

indicators.note: instils means puts in, so the piquancy goes inside the next piece

parts.note: down under is Australia, abbreviated Aus
spice is piquancy or zest

explanation.surface: Support from sponsors adds flavour in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their patronage or sponsorship.

clue.text: Vegetables plumbers called for

indicators.note: called for points to what is voiced: the thing plumbers are summoned for, as heard

parts.note: leaks are what plumbers come to fix

explanation.surface: Greengrocery that tradesmen were summoned to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumbers are called for leaks, which sound like the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeks are onion-family vegetables with long white stems.

clue.text: Where lager is brewed

indicators.note: brewed means mixed up in the making, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of which city a beer comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers, the Algerian capital, is a city, so it serves as a place where beer could be made.

clue.text: Film genre reportedly for culture vultures?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the film name is spoken

parts.note: Carry On was a long British series of comedy films, almost a genre in itself

explanation.surface: A kind of film that may appeal to arty types.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a British comedy series. 'Culture vultures' looks like arty people but means real vultures.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrion is the decaying flesh of dead animals, the food of literal vultures.

clue.text: Build or erect a building

indicators.note: building suggests the letters are assembled into a new structure

explanation.surface: Two ways to say put up a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build' and 'erect' both look like the definition; 'erect' is fodder and 'building' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to bring something into being, much as to build or construct it.

clue.text: She shows where to put your answer

definitions.text: She shows where to put your answer

parts.words: She shows where to put your answer
parts.note: a woman's name read as a phrase tells the solver the place in a crossword where answers are entered

explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN GRID, the name says where crossword answers go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's given name, so it fits 'She', while also splitting to describe the puzzle's grid.

clue.text: Cage none too soon?

parts.note: read as C for about (circa) plus AGE for time

explanation.surface: Locking something up at last.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) means about and an age is a time, so Cage is what ABOUT TIME would clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase about time is said when something happens late, meaning none too soon.

clue.text: Eager to top Welsh patron

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the top, so the first letter goes in this down answer

parts.note: St David is the patron saint of Wales

explanation.surface: Keen to outdo the patron saint of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager, especially for something one enjoys.

clue.text: Fish bounce ahead

indicators.note: a bounce sends a thing back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: read as a head, with nut slang for head

explanation.surface: A fish leaps forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'ahead' as 'a head', A NUT; 'bounce' turns it into TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean fish.

clue.text: Credo is a bitch

definitions.meaning: a creed or set of firmly held beliefs
a bitch is a female dog, which split jokingly makes a ..., a mother dog

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke: split the answer as DOG MA, a mother dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as true, which is what a credo states.

clue.text: This ran to no great advantage

definitions.text: This ran to no great advantage

parts.words: This ran to no great advantage
parts.note: put the word before 'ran' to get the phrase for a runner who finished nowhere, so it ran without much benefit

explanation.walkthrough: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that is unplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means too or as well, and joined to ran it names an unsuccessful runner.

clue.text: Wheeler, one who gets back nothing putting in nothing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: gets back means the piece is returned, read in reverse
putting in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: A cyclist who comes home with nothing after investing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting in' puts O inside NIX to make NOIX; 'gets back' turns it into XION, after I. Ixion was bound to a fiery wheel in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ixion was punished by being tied to a burning wheel forever, so he is a wheeler.

clue.text: American principles of taste

parts.note: the study of beauty and taste, given in the shorter US spelling without the leading A

explanation.walkthrough: Americans write the word without the initial A that British spelling keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophy of beauty and artistic taste is its field, here in the US spelling.
